findings.observed: The transitivity proof says that the individual sentences D_1 through D_m form a subset of Gamma: D_1, ..., D_m \subseteq Gamma.
findings.finding: A subset relation is applied to an unbraced list of sentence metavariables rather than to their set, creating a type and notation error.
controlling_evidence: The derivability definition quantifies a finite set of premises contained in Gamma.
The surrounding proof later uses each signed D_i as an assumption and concludes derivability from Gamma union Delta.
Each D_i therefore belongs to Gamma; alternatively the braced set of all D_i is a subset of Gamma.

findings.finding: The terminal index in the definition of the second finite premise set is copied from the first set and disagrees with the proof's own indexing.
controlling_evidence: Gamma_0 already uses B_1 through B_n.
The second displayed assumption set uses C_1 through C_m.
The later exhaustive-provability proof independently uses B_1 through B_n and C_1 through C_m for the same two-set construction.

findings.observed: The explicit-inconsistency proof contains a stray control-space after 'such that', applies the true-negation rule to the false-A conclusion rather than to the replacement true-not-A assumption, and redirects old line 1 to n+1 although the inserted false-A line follows n+1 assumptions.
findings.finding: Three local transcription errors obscure the otherwise uniquely determined tableau transformation and give its inserted conclusion the wrong premise and line number.
controlling_evidence: The named true-negation rule takes true not-A as premise and yields false A.
The construction replaces old assumption 1 by true not-A and retains the n premises B_1 through B_n, for n+1 assumptions in total.
Because false A is inserted after those assumptions, it is line n+2 and replaces every later appeal to old line 1.

findings.observed: Eight tableau result nodes call sFmla with the sentence nested inside the truth-sign argument and omit the required second argument.
findings.finding: Four true-conjunction result nodes and four false-disjunction result nodes use malformed one-argument signed-formula syntax.
controlling_evidence: Every well-formed signed formula in the chapter calls sFmla with a sign argument followed by a sentence argument.
The true-conjunction rule yields true A and true B on one branch.
The false-disjunction rule yields false A and false B on one branch.

findings.observed: The true-universal and false-universal soundness cases introduce schema B in five quantified-premise or satisfaction expressions, while their rule conclusions and subsequent arguments uniformly use schema A.
findings.finding: Five copied schema letters break the link between each universal premise and the instance whose satisfaction the proof establishes.
controlling_evidence: The true-universal case concludes true A(t) and invokes the quantifier-term proposition on A.
The false-universal case concludes false A(a) and carries A through the extension and sentence-satisfaction argument.
The general tableau rules instantiate the same formula schema appearing under the quantifier.
